nytimes_articles.abstract: Mayor Rudolph W Giuliani, with opening of school only two weeks away, raises possibility of compromise in his long-running battle with Board of Education over control of security in public schools; backing away from his demand that Police Dept be given complete authority over school safety, Giuliani says he will agree to let police run security in only some of city's 1,100 public schools (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: A Lovely Bit of Old China, Languishing in the New
nytimes_articles.abstract: Cuandixia, once wealthy mountain village 60 miles west of Beijing, offers peek into remarkable turmoil China has been through; its small parcels of tillable land are being abandoned as they become less able to yield income worth hoeing for, and young people are leaving for city in search of work; more than half of 70 stone-built homes in village are empty, and fewer than 50 people live there, or half number 10 years ago; photo; map (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Official Says Man Told Mob To 'Get a Jew'
nytimes_articles.abstract: Federal prosecutor Valerie Caproni, speaking at bail hearing for Charles Price, charges that he whipped group of blacks in Crown Heights into murderous frenzy five years ago and directed mob to kill Hasidic scholar Yankel Rosenbaum; Federal Magistrate John L Caden expresses skepticism about Government's attempt to link Price to killing (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: INTERNATIONAL MANAGER : Racing After Formula One Dollars
nytimes_articles.abstract: There's too much money in Formula One racing. At least that is the criticism increasingly used by those in the sport who don't have enough money to be competitive.. But as the role of money has increased in the sport, especially over the past decade, the

nytimes_articles.headline: 2 More Executives Leave Sunbeam
nytimes_articles.abstract: Rob Johnson leaves as president of Sunbeam Corp's household products group and Dan Lewis as vice president of group in latest management shakeup by new chairman and chief executive Albert J Dunlap (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Ciba-Geigy to Close Plant
nytimes_articles.abstract: Troubled Ciba-Geigy dye plant that once was Ocean County's largest private employer will close by end of 1996, Associated Press reports (New Jersey Daily Briefing) (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Garden Q.&A.
Volvo's First-Half Profits Topped Expectations
nytimes_articles.abstract: Volvo posts first-half pretax profit of 3.86 billion crowns ($585.3 million); says restructuring continues (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: In Some States, Planning Ahead Paid Off
nytimes_articles.abstract: Connecticut began to adopt new welfare program in July 1995; program, called Jobs First, involves 21-month limit on assistance to families--much tougher than five-year limit in new Federal law--and requirement that welfare recipients look for work; while Connecticut may need to make adjustments to comply with Federal guidelines, state officials are confident that thrust of their program satisfies basic Federal requirements (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: I.R.S., Now Meet the Reasonable Man
nytimes_articles.abstract: Teresa H Wyszomierski letter disputes J D Foster's Aug 19 Op-Ed article on Internal Revenue Service examiners; drawing (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: GE CAPITAL TO ACQUIRE STAKE IN AUTO-LEASING UNIT
nytimes_articles.abstract: General Electric Capital Corp, General Electric Co unit, to acquire 80 percent of Marubeni Car System; will buy 67 percent from Marubeni Corp, 6 percent from Orient Corp and remaining 7 percent from Yasuda Fire & Marine Insurance Co and Dai-Tokyo Fire & Marine Insurance Co (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Marines Arrive in Haiti in a Show of Force
nytimes_articles.abstract: US marines arrive in Haiti for routine training mission that becomes symbolic show of force following killing of two politicians and threat of more violence (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: French to Run Trains For London Commuters
nytimes_articles.abstract: Compagnie Generale des Eaux unit wins 15-year franchise to run most of southeast England's commuter train services into London; agrees to spend 400 million pounds ($619 million) on new trains (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Anti-Missile Issue
nytimes_articles.abstract: William Safire Op-Ed column says US should develop, test and deploy anti-missile system as defense against terrorists; says neither Clinton White House nor Defense Dept takes into defense planning possibility of theft or corrupt sale of nuclear missile to terrorists; says Clinton's defense policy is frozen in outdated cold-war strategy of Mutual Assured Destruction; welcomes Bob Dole support of missile defense (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Traffic Island Gardens for the East Village
nytimes_articles.abstract: Two gardens are planned for East Ninth Street in Manhattan where Third Avenue meets Ninth Street and Stuyvesant Street; drawing (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: CHRONICLE
nytimes_articles.abstract: Actor George Innes breaks his left leg during dress rehearsal for Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona at Globe Theater in London (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: The Pop Life
nytimes_articles.abstract: Pop Life column interviews Ike Turner, who is about to do his first concert in New York since 1975 and who is seeking to restore his reputation, which was damaged by the film based on Tina Turner's autobiography; photo; column also comments on the idea of a tribute album devoted to Big Star, an influential pop band of 1970's (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Helter-Shelter: New Look for Dream Books
nytimes_articles.abstract: Chrisopher Edley Jr Op-Ed article on welfare reform says liberals lost debate on welfare long ago, and lost it by losing debate on values (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: U.S. Petroleum Data
nytimes_articles.abstract: Table of United States petroleum data

nytimes_articles.headline: Groups Debate Sponsorship Of AIDS Fund-Raising Party
nytimes_articles.abstract: Drug overdose at Aug 18 party to raise funds to fight AIDS has intensified debate on whether Gay Men's Health Crisis should end its sponsorship of annual event on Fire Island (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: A Jumbotron Successor, as Big as the Law Allows
nytimes_articles.abstract: NBC and Panasonic executives plan to replace Times Square Jumbotron with something bigger and brighter; new screen, to be called Astrovision Giant Display Screen, will measure 891 square feet, largest allowed under New York City building codes; Jumbotron was removed by Sony Corp in June (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: NEW REPORT CITED ON CHEMICAL ARMS USED IN GULF WAR
nytimes_articles.abstract: Defense Dept acknowledges in new report that chemical weapons were detected as many as seven times in first week of 1991 Persian Gulf war with Iraq in stagging areas in northern Saudi Arabia, where tens of thousands of American troops were housed; while insisting that there is no conclusive evidence that US soldiers were ever exposed to Iraqi chemical weapons, Dept says it is exploring further plausibility that small amounts of chemical agents passed over American troops after bombers destroyed Iraqi arms depots and factories north of staging areas near Saudi city of Hafr al-Batin (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Clinton Book Repeats His Speeches
nytimes_articles.abstract: Pres Clinton's new book, Between Hope and History: Meeting America's Challenges for the 21st Century, written with William E Nothdurft, will be shipped to bookstores on Aug 22, with initial printing of 400,000 copies (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Clinton Writes Yeltsin on Grozny
nytimes_articles.abstract: Pres Clinton appeals to Pres Boris Yeltsin of Russia not to allow major military attack on Chechen capital of Grozny and to pursue negotiated settlement (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Japan's New Latin Look
nytimes_articles.abstract: Editorial comments on Japanese Prime Min Ryutaro Hashimoto's 10-day visit to Latin America; says while prospect of heightened Japanese competition may not delight American businesses operating there, companies should recognize that it is healthy for Latin American to broadan its international economic partnerships; says Japanese involvement sets good precedent for insisting that Japanese companies not try to lock American businesses out of Japan's booming East Asian neighborhood (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Clinton Backs The Military, Gore Asserts
nytimes_articles.abstract: Vice Pres Al Gore, in address to Veterans of Foreign Wars convention, defends Pres Clinton's commitment to military spending and to members of armed services; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Profits Decline 17% At Fried. Krupp
nytimes_articles.abstract: Fried Krupp AG reports first-half profits fell 17 percent, to 185 million marks ($124.2 million), down from 223 million marks in 1995 period (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Farrakhan Depicts Black Journalists as 'Slaves'
nytimes_articles.abstract: Louis Farrakhan, in address to National Association of Black Journalists, says black journalists are 'slaves' to white newspaper owners (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Arafat Rebuffs Israelis On Hebron Withdrawal
nytimes_articles.abstract: Yasir Arafat rejects Israeli linkage of troop redeployment in West Bank city of Hebron to halting of Palestinian activity in East Jerusalem; Israel says it will not withdraw troops from most of Hebron until Palestinian Authority closes PLO offices in Jerusalem (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Coffee Prices Rise as Colombia Increases Payments to Farmers
nytimes_articles.abstract: Coffee futures prices rise after Colombia raises amount it pays farmers by 17 percent in response to heavy rains that cut crop; coffee for Dec delivery rises 1.95 cents, to $1.17 a pound (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Running the Empire
nytimes_articles.abstract: C Webster Wheelock letter disputes Karl E Meyer's Aug 20 Editorial Notebook column on Morgan Library exhibit of works of late British artist/designer William Morris (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Economists' anti-regulatory rationale is facing a change.
nytimes_articles.abstract: Peter Passell economic scene article discusses shift in rationale of mainstream economists for opposing regulation; cites view of Peter Pitsch that likely benefits in taming corporate power pale beside costs in delaying and distorting innovation; drawing (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Growing Fears in Britain Of Single-Currency Isolation
nytimes_articles.abstract: British financial executives and business economists are concerned about impact should Britain delay joining European Monetary Union, set to adopt single currency and central bank in Jan 1999; Britain is one of few European nations whose recent economic performance qualifies it for membership, but has retained right to opt out of union and seeks to dodge politically-charged issue (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: U.N. Hears Conflicting Views on What to Do About Burundi
nytimes_articles.abstract: Leaders of opposing political parties in Burundi arrive in New York to brief United Nations Council and to try to influence what course it will take in wake of recent coup that overthrew democratically elected Govt (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: It's a Loyal Ally but May Dig Up Trouble
nytimes_articles.abstract: Article on dispute between Manhattan Borough Pres Ruth W Messinger and Parks Comr Howard J Stern over his plan to use city employees to count how many times his dog, Boomer, is petted so he can get dog into Guinness Book of World Records as world's most petted dog; photos of Boomer and other politicians' pets (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: 'Primary Colors': Second Thoughts
nytimes_articles.abstract: Tom Hanks's decision not to portray Bill Clinton in the film Primary Colors startles the director, Mike Nichols, and studio, Universal; Jeffrey Seller, one of producers of the Broadway musical Rent, insists that while the family of the show's composer, the late Jonathan Larson, owns the film rights, any film deal hinges on the concurrence of the four producers; Miramax has announced a film deal (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Central Board Backs All-Girls School
nytimes_articles.abstract: Board of Education votes to endorse Young Women's Leadership School, all-girls junior high school that will open in East Harlem community school district, and to expand it into all-girls high school that board and district will operate jointly; New York Civil Rights Coalition exec dir Michael Meyers says he will file complaint with US Education Dept, seeking to block school from opening on Sept 4 (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Common Drug for Prostrate Is Ineffective, Study Finds
nytimes_articles.abstract: First direct comparison of terazosin and hytrin, two main drugs used for treating enlarged prostate gland, found hytrin was effective in relieving urinary symptons caused when swollen gland restricts urethra, but that terazosin is no better than dummy pill or placebo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: But Questions Persist On Risks of Reinsurance
nytimes_articles.abstract: Lloyd's of London 'names,' individuals who pledge their assets to back insurance policies sold at Lloyds, are expected to approve plan to restore British insurance market to solvency by shifting billions of dollars of liabilities to Equitas, newly formed reinsurance firm; will pay up to $150,000 each to help capitalize Equitas and Lloyds will contribute some 3.2 billion pounds (almost $5 billion), freeing it of liability for claims arising from outstanding policies written before 1993; policyholders and insurance experts worry Equitas, even with $19.5 billion in reserves, will not have adequate resources; Lloyds chief executive Ron Sandler holds Equitas is 'extremely unlikely' to fail, interview; diagram; drawings; photo (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Accounts
In Russian, Even Words Hold Music
nytimes_articles.abstract: Anthony Tommasini reviews three albums of Russian vocal music performed by Sergei Leiferkus, Sergej Larin and Dmitri Hvorostovsky; photos (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: F.C.C. Eases Equal-Time Rule for 3 Networks
nytimes_articles.abstract: Federal Communications Commission says it will permit some television networks to choose which candidates they will grant free broadcast time to during Presidential campaign; commission, by permitting networks to exclude minor candidates, clears potential obstacle to efforts to secure uniform free time for major party Presidential candidates (M)
